IncidentBot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'west-dedicated-03' p95/p99 latency breach detected in us-west-2 — queue depth spike + sustained warmup lag. Trigger: latency-slo-checker. Severity: paged.
Devon (oncall): ack — paging in. seeing a big tail at p99 (~4.2s) and streaming stalls in the telemetry graph. I'll grab metrics and triage.
Devon (oncall): quick hit: queue_depth: 420 -> backlog, autoscaler lagging: scale_decision_time ~3m. recent config change? :thinking_face:
AJ (sre): I can join — switching to triage channel. Can you paste the autoscaler logs and pool allocation timeline?
Devon (oncall): paste logs below (truncated):
```
2026-03-15T02:00:10Z pool=west-dedicated-03 queue_depth=18 scale_signal=add-slot
2026-03-15T02:00:20Z pool=west-dedicated-03 queue_depth=120 scale_signal=add-slot
2026-03-15T02:02:05Z pool=west-dedicated-03 scale_action=start_slots=6 reason=handshake_warmup
2026-03-15T02:05:30Z pool=west-dedicated-03 queue_depth=380 autoscaler_state=waiting telemetry_agg_delay=130s
```
Devon (oncall): note the telemetry aggregation delay value — autoscaler is using an aggregated metric stream that lagged behind real-time by ~2m, causing late scale decisions.
Kevin (runtime): I see repeated 'warmup' failures on new slots: kv_cache miss spike and model init latencies high. worker-init memory pressure on machines that got churned earlier.
Nate (eng): Also seeing elevated disk IO in those hosts — we had a maintenance job moving cgroup logs earlier, might have increased IO wait. Not sure if correlated.
AJ (sre): For immediate mitigation: (1) enable conservative fallback routing to warm pool (west-dedicated-01) for streaming endpoints, (2) temporarily increase autoscaler aggressiveness threshold, (3) mark new slot warmup as tolerable (increase warmup timeout) to avoid thrashing.
Devon (oncall): Doing (1) now — running rollout command to shift 30% of streaming traffic to warm pool.
Devon (oncall): `/infra traffic-route set --from pool:west-dedicated-03 --to pool:west-dedicated-01 --percent 30 --reason "latency surge fallback"`
IncidentBot: Deploy job queued: rollout-id=rl-20260315-237; started
Devon (oncall): (2) bumping autoscaler aggressiveness: `/infra autoscaler update west-dedicated-03 --scale-factor 1.6 --max-ramp 8` — applied.
Kevin (runtime): I'm investigating worker init logs — found repeated OOM-ish events during model load for q8 variants. Increasing model-load-parallelism to 2 to reduce concurrent memory pressure.
Nate (eng): I'm kicking off a small host drain on 3 noisy hosts (id: host-az3-07, host-az3-09, host-az3-11) to reduce IO pressure. Will reattach later.
Devon (oncall): Customer impact check: streaming sessions with long prompt + long output show stalls and reconnects. Product metrics: affected requests ~12% of streaming traffic in region, error rates at peak +8% above baseline, tail latency p99 bumped to ~4.2s.
Maria (product): Which customers are impacted? Any enterprise tenants on dedicated pools? Need to notify support if customer SLA risk.
Devon (oncall): Quick lookup: three active enterprise tenants mapped to this pool (acct-A, acct-B, acct-C). acct-A shows increased user-visible retries; acct-B has some webhook delivery timeouts; acct-C intermittent stalls during streaming.
Maria (product): I'll draft a customer message: short note + mitigations and ETA. tagging support lead.
AJ (sre): Observed root contributors so far: telemetry aggregation delay causing late autoscaler actions, warmup latency on new slots (model load + KV priming), and host-level IO causing worker stutter. Need mitigation + postmortem.
Kevin (runtime): Short term: enable prefix caching for hot models to reduce kv priming time; flipping on `prefix_cache=true` for the hot model group now.
Devon (oncall): Confirming prefix_cache toggle applied. Watching if p95 improves.
Devon (oncall): Rolling increase of surge capacity initiated: started 6 new slots at 02:06:40Z — but warmup completion times vary (40s-3m) depending on host.
AJ (sre): If warmup variance stays high, we'll keep fallback routing in place until p99 normalizes. Also will lower telemetry agg window for autoscaler to 15s from 60s temporarily (risk: noise), to make decisions more real-time.
Devon (oncall): Done: autoscaler telemetry window set to 15s. Observing faster scale actions now.
IncidentBot: Note added to incident timeline by Devon (oncall): "fallback routing applied, autoscaler telemetry window reduced, noisy hosts draining".
Devon (oncall): Current status (02:11Z): queue_depth down to 95, p95 latency ~1.2s, p99 trending down from 4.2s -> 2.1s. Streaming stalls significantly reduced but not fully cleared.
Maria (product): Good, please keep me posted. I'll prepare customer comms: short impact + root cause + mitigation steps + ETA for full recovery.
AJ (sre): Action items assigned: AJ — continue autoscaler tuning and confirm stability; Kevin — follow model-init memory tuning and confirm no more OOMs; Nate — complete host drains and validate IO health; Devon — customer triage + keep incident doc updated. Postmortem owner: Devon.
Devon (oncall): Handoff: I'm on-call until 02:30Z. AJ will take the 02:30-06:00Z window for follow-up and postmortem write-up.
AJ (sre): I'll pick up at 02:30. If anything regresses ping me direct @aj.sre.
Devon (oncall): closing the live paging loop for now — continuing monitoring. Please escalate if p99 creeps back above 3s.
IncidentBot: Incident severity updated -> mitigated (partial). Pager cleared.
Devon (oncall): Post-incident notes: suspect telemetry aggregator had a delayed push due to batch window + maintenance job; warmup sensitivity needs tuning; consider autoscaler canary for telemetry drift checks. Will include in postmortem.
Maria (product): Thanks team. Support will notify impacted accounts with the initial message and we'll follow up with postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
AJ (sre): filing a quick follow-up task: `SRE-5234` — autoscaler telemetry alerting + reduce agg-delay risk. Assigning to AJ.
Devon (oncall): End of thread for now.
